claim: Influenza is responsible for an estimated 250,000–500,000 deaths each year worldwide.
source: Influenza remains one of the major threats to human health worldwide and is responsible for an estimated 250,000–500,000 deaths each year (World Health Organization, 2009).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to the World Health Organization, 2009.

claim: Attempts at influenza immunization pre-dated the isolation of the virus from humans in 1933.
source: Attempts at immunization pre-dated the isolation of the virus from humans in 1933 (Smith et al., 1933)
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Smith et al., 1933.

claim: Vaccination remains the cornerstone of influenza prevention strategies.

evidence: This is a statement of established scientific consensus about influenza prevention.

claim: Since 1977, strains of influenza A (H3N2), influenza A (H1N1), and influenza B have been responsible for the majority of documented human infections.

claim: Trivalent influenza vaccines are updated annually to contain the circulating strains.

claim: Animal models have demonstrated that immune responses to influenza infection can be strongly influenced by host genetic factors.

claim: Animal models have demonstrated that susceptibility to influenza infection can be strongly influenced by host genetic factors.

claim: Variability in the immune response to vaccination is likely to be influenced by genotype.
